chapterTitle: Know WHY. Know HOW. Then WHAT?
focus: As a cause scales into an organization, the leader becomes the source of WHY, senior operators translate HOW, and front-line outputs communicate WHAT to the world.
coreClaim: Organizations function as megaphones for a leader's WHY only when the message remains clear from source through systems to visible actions.

centralConcept.name: organization as megaphone
centralConcept.plainDefinition: The Golden Circle becomes a three-dimensional cone: WHY at the top, HOW in the middle, WHAT at the base. The marketplace encounters the base, so products, service, advertising, and employee behavior must carry the original belief outward.
centralConcept.whyItMatters: A reader who uses this model can see why scale distorts purpose. The leader no longer speaks to everyone directly, so the organization must translate the cause without muddying it.

keyClaims: The leader's job is to personify and protect the WHY, not to personally perform every WHAT.
Senior leaders and managers operate in the HOW layer by building systems, standards, and teams that embody the belief.
Most employees and market-facing artifacts sit at the WHAT layer, where outsiders actually hear and see the organization.
A loud megaphone cannot compensate for an unclear message at the source.
Advertising and public relations amplify meaning only when the WHATs already prove the belief.
The marketplace is noisy and disorganized, so repeated clear signals matter more than occasional clever campaigns.
Symbols, stories, products, and service moments all become carriers of the same underlying cause.

namedExamples.label: Apple's 1984 commercial and Think Different campaign
namedExamples.summary: Apple's famous launch advertising and later rebel-themed campaign are treated as expressions of the same individual-empowerment belief. The ads are not presented as feature lists; they make the company's cause visible through symbols, story, and tone.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: Marketing works as proof when creative choices embody the WHY instead of merely decorating the product.

namedExamples.label: Martin Luther King Jr.'s movement infrastructure
namedExamples.summary: A leader with a cause still needed organizers, churches, local networks, and public events to carry the message beyond one voice. The organization around the cause served as a living amplifier.
namedExamples.teachesWhat: A message reaches scale through structures that translate belief into repeatable public action.

hardEdge: The tempting mistake is to think communication means louder advertising, more channels, or a better tagline. The harder lesson is transmission discipline: scale helps only when the leader's WHY, the operators' HOW, and the visible WHAT all carry the same signal.
voiceCues: turns a flat diagram into a three-dimensional organizational metaphor
uses megaphone language to connect leadership clarity with market communication
moves from hierarchy to marketplace contact points
keeps Apple advertising as evidence of belief-led expression
paraphraseNotes: The circle becomes a cone once people organize around the cause. At the top sits the source of WHY: a leader or founding belief that gives direction and meaning. The middle layer contains HOW-types and senior operators who build the systems, standards, incentives, and hiring logic that translate belief into practice. The base is the WHAT layer: employees, products, service, marketing, storefronts, packaging, and every public contact with the marketplace. Outsiders rarely touch the top directly. They encounter the base and infer the cause from what they see. That makes the organization a megaphone. A clear source amplified through disciplined systems can reach a chaotic market with a recognizable signal. An unclear source simply gets louder and more confusing. Apple's 1984 commercial and Think Different campaign show advertising used as proof of an existing belief rather than as a substitute for one. Martin Luther King Jr.'s public leadership also needed churches, organizers, marches, and networks to project the cause beyond a single speaker. The communication problem is therefore structural, not just verbal. Scale demands translation without dilution: WHY to HOW to WHAT, then outward into a market that only sees tangible evidence.
